project.name: Job Intelligence Platform
project.description: Personal career intelligence platform for discovering, normalizing, evaluating, tracking and analyzing jobs.

items.title: Canonical Job / Job Listing
items.description: Create one canonical Job identity with one or more source listings, so the same opportunity is never represented as duplicate tracked Jobs.
acceptance: One job can have multiple source listings.
A duplicate job cannot be created merely because the URL or source differs.
Each listing retains its own source and URL.

acceptanceCriteria.check: Add the same opportunity from two sources
acceptanceCriteria.expect: One canonical Job is retained and both source listings are attached.
verify: Each listing retains source and URL.
failureCases: Different source listings create duplicate Jobs.
Deleting one listing unexpectedly deletes the canonical Job.

acceptanceCriteria.check: Open a Job from a source listing
acceptanceCriteria.expect: The canonical Job opens and the originating source/listing remains visible.

items.title: Source URL and Company Identity
items.description: Identify the source domain and company name primarily from normalized URL, HTML title and page content while keeping source type as a user-controlled classification.
acceptance: Company name can be identified where possible.
Source identity is based on normalized domain/source title rather than individual job paths.
User can correct the company/source name and type.

acceptanceCriteria.expect: Company source is identified as the company domain and the job path remains a listing URL.
Board source is identified while the individual job URL remains separate.
failureCases: Every job URL becomes a source.

items.title: Referral and Final Publisher Resolution
items.description: Handle jobs discovered through one source that redirect to a different company or job-board publisher.
acceptance: Original referral source remains available.
Final publisher source is identified.
User can correct the final source.
The Job is not duplicated because of the referral.

acceptanceCriteria.check: Referral URL redirects to company Job
acceptanceCriteria.expect: Final company source is used for publishing identity while referral provenance remains.

acceptance: Known sources are preloaded.

acceptanceCriteria.expect: Known sources exist once and remain stable.

items.title: Job Source
items.description: Create a reliable Job Source registry where one normalized source can contain many jobs.
acceptance: User can add a source.

acceptanceCriteria.expect: LinkedIn is created or matched as one Job Source.
failureCases: Individual job URL becomes the source identity.

acceptanceCriteria.expect: Both jobs belong under the same source.
verify: Each job retains its own listing URL.

acceptanceCriteria.check: Create source from a new URL

failureCases: Incorrect automatic classification cannot be corrected.

Results can be aggregated by email sender or Job Source.

items.title: Email Source Recommendation Analytics
items.description: Measure which Job Sources and email senders provide useful recommendations based on the user's profile, interactions and application history.
acceptance: The system can show recommendation counts by email sender or Job Source.
The system can show how many recommendations were relevant.
The system can show how many recommendations were saved.
The system can show how many recommendations resulted in applications.
The system can identify sources that repeatedly produce irrelevant recommendations.
The analytics are based on observed data rather than an arbitrary source ranking.

items.title: Email Source Cleanup and Blocking
items.description: Allow the user to identify unwanted job recommendation sources and manage them through an explicit block or cleanup workflow.
acceptance: The user can identify email sources producing unwanted recommendations.
A source can be marked as unwanted.
Blocked sources can be excluded from future recommendation processing.
The system can identify previously received messages from a blocked source.
Blocking a source does not delete canonical Jobs or Applications already stored.
Email deletion or mailbox-level filtering remains controlled by the user's email provider or n8n workflow.

items.title: Email Application Feedback Matching
items.description: Match incoming application-related emails against Jobs and Applications already tracked in JobIntel.
acceptance: Incoming application emails can be matched to a known Job where sufficient evidence exists.
The system can identify likely application feedback.
Matching uses multiple signals such as company, title, source, URL, recruiter and application context.
Ambiguous matches are presented for confirmation instead of silently changing an Application.
Unmatched emails remain available for manual review.

items.title: Automatic Application Stage Detection
items.description: Use incoming application emails to identify possible changes in application stage.
acceptance: The system can recognize common application events such as screening, interview invitation, rejection, offer and withdrawal.
Detected stages are associated with the correct Application where confidence is sufficient.
Automatic changes are auditable.
Ambiguous stage changes require user confirmation.
The existing ApplicationStage history is preserved.
The system never replaces historical stages merely because a new email was received.

items.title: Email Tag Synchronization
items.description: Synchronize relevant email tags or labels with JobIntel application and Job states where the user's email provider supports it.
acceptance: Configured email labels can represent supported JobIntel states.
Application feedback can update the configured email label.
JobIntel status changes can optionally update the corresponding email label.
Synchronization is idempotent.
Email synchronization failures do not change the canonical Job or Application incorrectly.
The user can see whether synchronization succeeded or failed.

items.title: Email-to-Job Recommendation Workflow
items.description: Turn relevant job recommendation emails into controlled discovery records that follow the same Job, Job Source and duplicate rules as other ingestion methods.
acceptance: Email recommendations can enter the Discovery system.
Email ingestion does not bypass duplicate Job detection.
The publishing Job Source can be identified where possible.
Unknown publishing sources can use Unclassified Source.
The user can review an email-derived opportunity before promoting it to a Job.
Email remains an acquisition method distinct from the Job Source.

items.title: Job Source Directory
items.description: Provide a dedicated Job Sources page containing all Job Sources known to the system.
acceptance: All active Job Sources can be viewed.
Archived or disabled sources can be filtered separately.
Sources can be filtered by SourceType.
Sources can be filtered by risk status.
Sources can be filtered by paid/free status.
Each source links to its source workspace.

items.title: Job Source Paid Status
items.description: Record whether a Job Source requires payment or subscription before or after applying for Jobs.
acceptance: A Job Source can be marked as free.
A Job Source can be marked as requiring payment before applying.
A Job Source can be marked as requiring payment after applying.
The payment classification is visible in the Job Source workspace.
The classification can be manually corrected.
Payment status is not confused with Job application status.

items.title: Job Source Response Behaviour
items.description: Track observed response behaviour for Job Sources, including whether applications tend to receive responses and how quickly responses occur.
acceptance: The system records application response events.
Response timing can be calculated from application and response timestamps.
A Job Source can show observed response behaviour.
The system distinguishes no response from a known delayed response.
Response behaviour is based on the user's observed applications rather than a universal claim about the source.

items.title: Public Landing Page
items.description: Introduce a public landing page explaining JobIntel, its core capabilities and how the system helps manage job discovery and applications.
acceptance: Unauthenticated users can access the landing page.
The page explains Job discovery, source tracking, application tracking and career intelligence.
The page does not expose private Jobs, Applications, CVs or user data.
The page provides a clear route to sign in.
The page works independently of the authenticated application shell.

items.title: Public Job Source Showcase
items.description: Provide a public-facing Job Sources page showing the source directory information that is safe to expose.
acceptance: The public page can show configured public Job Sources.
Private user-specific information is excluded.
Public source information can include SourceType and configured risk/payment indicators where appropriate.
Source links open the correct public source homepage.
The page does not expose private application or CV data.

items.title: Recent Job Source Highlights
items.description: Show a small set of recent Jobs grouped by relevant Job Source categories on the solo-user landing experience.
acceptance: The page can show recent Jobs from configured categories.
The number of displayed Jobs can be limited to a small configured amount such as six per category.
Only appropriate public Job data is displayed.
Expired, closed or risky Jobs follow the configured display policy.
The list links to the appropriate Job details.

items.title: EJS Job Sharing Email Template
items.description: Replace the basic Job sharing email with a structured EJS template containing useful Job and source information.
acceptance: The sharing email is rendered through EJS.
The template includes the Job title.
The template includes company information.
The template includes relevant source and URL information.
The template includes risk information where appropriate.
The email renders correctly in common email clients.
Missing optional Job fields do not break rendering.

items.title: Forgot Password
items.description: Provide a password recovery workflow suitable for the current single-user system.
acceptance: The user can request password recovery.
A recovery code is sent to the configured account email.
The code has an expiration time.
Expired or already-used codes are rejected.
The password can be reset after successful verification.
Password reset events are logged appropriately.
The workflow does not expose whether unrelated email addresses exist.

items.title: Single-User Email Code Authentication
items.description: For the current solo deployment, replace public registration with controlled email-code authentication.
acceptance: Public registration is removed from the normal user-facing flow.
The configured account email can request a sign-in code.
Only valid unexpired codes authenticate the account.
Codes are single-use.
Repeated failed attempts are rate limited.
Authentication events are logged.
The architecture leaves room for future multi-user authentication.

items.title: Authentication CAPTCHA Protection
items.description: Add CAPTCHA protection to appropriate authentication and recovery entry points.
acceptance: CAPTCHA is displayed on configured authentication/recovery flows.
The backend validates CAPTCHA rather than trusting the frontend.
Failed CAPTCHA verification prevents the protected action.
CAPTCHA failure is handled without exposing sensitive account information.
CAPTCHA can be disabled or configured appropriately for local development.

items.title: Public Demo Environment
items.description: Provide a safe demo version of JobIntel for people who want to explore the product without accessing the real user's data.
acceptance: The demo uses isolated demo data.
Real user Jobs, Applications, CVs and credentials are inaccessible.
Demo users cannot modify production data.
The demo can demonstrate Job discovery, source management, applications and reporting.
Demo reset or data refresh is supported.
The demo environment has appropriate rate limits and security controls.

items.title: Contribution and Expansion Intake
items.description: Create a controlled mechanism for collecting contributions and proposals if JobIntel is later opened to collaborators.
acceptance: The project can publish contribution guidelines.
Potential contributors can submit feature or improvement proposals.
Contribution requests are separated from production access.
The current solo-user architecture remains protected.
The process can later support additional maintainers or administrators.

items.title: Multi-User and Role-Based Expansion Plan
items.description: Prepare the architecture for possible expansion from the current solo system into a multi-user platform with administrators and role-based permissions.
acceptance: Current single-user authentication remains supported.
Future user isolation requirements are documented.
Administrative capabilities are identified separately from normal user capabilities.
Role and permission boundaries are documented before implementation.
Private user data is designed to remain isolated between future accounts.
The current system does not introduce unnecessary multi-user complexity before it is required.
